rules.title: San Francisco ban on algorithmic rent-setting tools
rules.requirement: Property owners and managers in San Francisco may not use algorithm-based tools that recommend or set rental prices.
rules.key_value: Ban on algorithm-based tools that recommend or set rents
rules.coverage_conditions: Property owners and managers of residential rental housing in San Francisco.
rules.citation: San Francisco Board of Supervisors legislation approved July 2024 (citation not given in document)
rules.quoted_span:
In July 2024, the San Francisco Board of Supervisors approved 
legislation to ban property owners and managers from using algorithm-based tools that recommend 
or set rental prices.

rules.title: Motion to study a ban on algorithm-based rent-setting software (CF 24-1031)
rules.requirement: Proposal only: the City Council would instruct LAHD to report on landlords using algorithmic rent-setting software and the feasibility of banning it. No ban is in effect under this document.
rules.key_value: Report on feasibility of banning algorithmic rent-setting software
rules.coverage_conditions: Ownership and management entities of rental housing in the City of Los Angeles using algorithm-based software to set rents.
rules.quoted_span:
I THEREFORE MOVE that the City Council instruct the Los Angeles Housing Department to 
report on the number of ownership and management entities that are using algorithm-based 
software to establish rents and the feasibility of instituting a ban on the use of this software to set 
rents in the City.

notes: D039 is a Los Angeles City Council motion (CF 24-1031, Sept. 3, 2024). It only asks the Housing Department to report on algorithmic rent-setting software and whether a ban is feasible. It does not ban anything. It is recorded as pending, but this document does not show whether the motion is still alive as of 2026-10-01, or whether an ordinance followed. Check the council file history. The San Francisco ban comes from a passing mention in the motion. The document gives no ordinance number, citation or effective date. 'in_force' is inferred from the July 2024 approval and should be checked against the enacted SF ordinance. The mentions of DOJ, DC and Arizona actions involve agencies or places outside the jurisdictions in scope and were left out.
